terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: The terms that apply when you use America.gov.

paragraphs.1: These Terms of Use apply to America.gov and to the tools and answers served through it. America.gov is an official service of the United States government, operated by the General Services Administration.
paragraphs.2: By using America.gov you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the site. We may change these terms as the service changes, and the date at the top of this page tells you when it was last updated.

service.heading: What America.gov does and does not do

paragraphs.1: America.gov helps you find government information and understand the steps for government tasks. It explains information and links to the agency that owns a program. Asking a question here does not submit an application, file a document, or contact an agency on your behalf.
paragraphs.2: America.gov is not the agency of record. It does not decide your eligibility, approve a benefit, or change a filing. Only the responsible agency can do that, and the agency’s own determination always controls.

paragraphs.1: Some answers on America.gov are generated with AI. They can be incomplete or wrong, and they can be out of date the moment a program changes.
paragraphs.2: Check the linked source before you act on an answer, especially for anything involving money, immigration status, benefits, or a deadline. Nothing here is legal, tax, medical, or financial advice.

paragraphs.1: Use America.gov for its intended purpose. Do not attempt to gain unauthorized access to any part of the service, probe or test its security, or interfere with how it works for other people.
paragraphs.2: Do not use automated tools to scrape the site, place an unreasonable load on it, misrepresent who you are, or use the service to carry out anything unlawful. We may block activity that does any of these things.

paragraphs.1: Most content on America.gov is a work of the United States government and is in the public domain. You may use it freely, and you do not need our permission to do so.
paragraphs.2: Some material is not ours to license, including third-party logos, trademarks, photographs, and agency seals. Do not use a government seal or logo in a way that suggests endorsement of your product, service, or organization.

paragraphs.1: America.gov links to federal, state, local, tribal, and non-government sites when they are the best answer to your question. A link is not an endorsement.
paragraphs.2: Once you leave America.gov, the terms and privacy practices of that site apply. We do not control their content and are not responsible for it.

paragraphs.1: America.gov is provided as is. We work to keep it accurate and available, but we do not warrant that it will be error-free, uninterrupted, or fit for a particular purpose.
paragraphs.2: To the extent allowed by law, the United States government is not liable for any loss that results from your use of the site or from reliance on an answer it gives you.

paragraphs.1: We will post any change to these terms on this page and update the date at the top. Continuing to use America.gov after a change means you accept the updated terms.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What America.gov collects, how it is used, and the choices you have.

paragraphs.1: America.gov is operated by the General Services Administration (GSA). This policy covers America.gov, including the chat surface (“chat”) and the pages served under this domain. It explains what we collect, why we collect it, and what we do with it.
paragraphs.2: Other government sites we link to have their own privacy policies. When you leave America.gov, this policy stops applying.

input.heading: 2. Your questions, attachments, and voice input

paragraphs.1: You can browse America.gov without telling us who you are. We do not ask you to create an account to get an answer.
paragraphs.2: You can use America.gov without giving us personal information. You choose what to include in your question or attachment.

paragraphs.1: When you ask a question, we process what you type so we can answer it. The application does not save chat history or include message text in its usage analytics unless you explicitly provide feedback using the thumbs up/thumbs down icons.
paragraphs.2: Your conversation and pending questions are held in browser memory. America.gov does not save them as an account history. Your browser may preserve the page and its conversation when you navigate away and return using the Back button.
paragraphs.3: When you ask a question to <america>America.gov</america>, our AI model performs searches across government websites in a secure, sandboxed version of the Internet.

paragraphs.1: If you attach a PDF, we extract its text in your browser. Avoid sending PDFs that contain personally identifiable information (PII).
paragraphs.2: When a file is uploaded, we will make a best-effort attempt in your browser to remove any private details using <rampart>Rampart</rampart> (an open-source classifier system to detect some types of PII, such as Social Security Numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, and credit card numbers).

paragraphs.1: America.gov uses your browser’s built-in speech recognition to convert speech into text. The provider depends on your browser and operating system—for example, Google in Chrome, Apple in Safari, or Microsoft Azure in desktop Edge.
paragraphs.2: Your browser may send microphone audio directly to that provider for transcription under its privacy practices. America.gov’s servers receive the resulting text, which we process like text you type. You can choose to type instead.

paragraphs.1: We receive technical information with requests, including the requested URL, network address, date and time, and headers your browser sends. Application metrics record request routes, response status, timing, and errors.
paragraphs.2: We use your IP address to keep the service available and to stop abuse via automated rate limiting. If you hit a rate limit, the address appears in Cloudflare security logs.

paragraphs.1: To include results relevant to your area, we may send our AI providers your general area (such as your city or region), estimated from your network address. This estimate is approximate; we do not use GPS or ask your browser for your precise location.

The application does not save language preferences, questions, or diagnostic preferences to cookies, local storage, or session storage. Your language selection is included in the page URL and can persist when you reload, bookmark, or share that URL.
paragraphs.2: The application removes legacy preferences and pending questions saved by earlier versions. You can also clear site data in your browser settings. Questions included in a page URL can appear in browser history.

paragraphs.1: We do not use advertising cookies or third-party trackers, and we do not currently participate in federal web analytics programs.

retention.heading: 5. Information we store and how long we keep it

paragraphs.1: Our feedback form does not ask for your name, email address, or other personal information. When you choose to give us feedback, we store your rating and comments, along with the AI-generated response, sources, and metadata, for up to one year to improve our product. Please do not include personal information in your comments.

We record operational measurements, including pseudonymous identifiers, model and tool outcomes, timing, and token counts, to understand usage and improve reliability. We store this for up to 90 days.

To improve performance, we store AI-generated responses in Cloudflare KV for up to two hours. We store only a hash of the prompt as the cache key, not the prompt text. The cached response itself is not hashed. We may store search results our AI performs for up to two hours and generated follow-up suggestions for up to 30 days for faster responses.

We retain Cloudflare security logs, which may include your IP address, for 12 months. Separately, Cloudflare’s published Enterprise retention limits are up to 30 days for its Security Events dataset and up to 90 days for its Security Analytics dataset.

We share information you provide with the vendors who run the infrastructure behind this service under contract to the government. Our AI providers operate under Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreements and retain none of your prompts or the responses they generate. America.gov’s own response cache is separate and is described in Section 5.
paragraphs.2: Our AI providers are contractually prohibited from selling your information, building an advertising profile, or training their AI models with your data.

paragraphs.1: We may also share information when we are required to by law, or when it is necessary to investigate a security incident or an attempt to misuse the service.

The America.gov team implements industry-standard security measures in compliance with federal information security regulations; this includes encryption and access controls to protect and isolate user data from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.
We will post any change to this policy on this page and update the date at the top.

mistakes.body: This website uses AI to find and explain government agency information based on available official sources. AI may miss details or misinterpret guidance, and sources may be incomplete or out of date. Check the linked sources before making decisions.

gsa.question: What is the General Services Administration?
gsa.answer: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is the federal agency that provides technology, workplaces, purchasing services, and shared tools for federal agencies. GSA operates America.gov. Learn more about GSA

studio.question: What is National Design Studio?
studio.answer: The National Design Studio is a White House team established by Executive Order 14338. It brings design and technology experts into public service to make government services clearer, simpler, and easier to use.

inaccurate.question: What if an answer is inaccurate?
inaccurate.answer: America.gov uses AI to find and explain information from official government sources. AI can make mistakes, so check the sources included with each answer before making an important decision. To report a problem, select the feedback button below the answer and describe what was incorrect or out of date.

on-behalf.question: Can I ask questions on behalf of someone else?
on-behalf.answer: Yes. You can ask general questions for a family member, friend, or someone you support. Please do not share their personal or sensitive information.

contact.question: How can I contact America.gov?
contact.answer: Select the thumbs-up or thumbs-down icon below any answer to tell us what worked or report a problem. America.gov does not currently offer phone support. For help with a specific government program or application, contact the agency responsible for it.

app.question: Will there be an America.gov app?
app.answer: There is no separate app today. America.gov works in a web browser on phones, tablets, and computers.

neutrality.question: Is America.gov politically neutral?
neutrality.answer: America.gov does not provide campaign or party information. Its answers are based on published government sources, and you can review those sources yourself.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No. You do not need an account to use America.gov or ask a question. It does not ask you to identify yourself, and you should avoid sharing personal information. See the Privacy Policy for more details.

application-status.question: Can I check the status of an application?
application-status.answer: Not currently. America.gov cannot access agency records or see applications you have submitted. It can help you find the responsible agency’s official status-checking tool.

websites.question: What does “29,000 government websites” mean?
websites.answer: The government publishes information across thousands of websites managed by many different agencies and offices. America.gov helps you find and understand that information without needing to know which website to visit first.
